rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from the sky and stars to the earth, naming the seas and graves as the next signs of the upheaval.
rows.anchor: After a mention of the sky and its stars, the state of the two things

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea term has the same meaning as the previous sūrah’s term, but the former stresses the seas’ unrestrained spread and the latter their tumult.
rows.anchor: unrestrained nature of the seas

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection the seas will break their present bounds and spread across the land; the author previously explained this under al-Dahr 76:6.
rows.anchor: the seas at the advent of the Day of Judgement will cross their current limits and spread over the crest and fall of the land.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for graves opening means to scatter, tear open, or open something and take out what is inside.
rows.anchor: “to scatter and disperse something,” “to tear open something,” “to open something and take out whatever is in it.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Graves are singled out because the prospect of people being exhumed is especially effective as a warning; other verses say the earth casts out all its burdens.
rows.anchor: Only graves are mentioned in this verse because their mention and the mention of the fact

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel about the Jews says they know their deeds and lack courage to face God, illustrating the knowledge of what a person has sent ahead.
rows.anchor: they do not have the courage to face the Almighty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the arrogant addressees, the phrase means they will face the consequences of evils they intended against God and His Messenger and yearn for good deeds they neglected; parallel verses show regret over their deeds.
rows.anchor: the yearning of good deeds which they had ignored.

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some interpret what is sent ahead and left behind as all good or evil deeds a person did or could not do.
rows.anchor: whatever good or evil he did or could not do

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation concerns wealth sent to the next world and wealth left for heirs.
rows.anchor: what he sent forth from his wealth to the next world and what he left behind from it for his heirs

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the alternatives fit the verse’s general sense, the author prefers his interpretation because of the context and placement.
rows.anchor: I, in the light of its context and placement, would give preference to the interpretation I have made.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s power, creativity, care, and wisdom in creating humanity show that He acted purposefully and will hold people accountable, resurrecting and judging them.
rows.anchor: power, creativity, thoroughness and wisdom in creating

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation vocabulary spans making or sketching and creating, then perfecting; the verses thus allude to humanity’s initial and final stages of formation.
rows.anchor: “to make a sketch of something” and “to create something”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s continued respite is benevolence, but the disbelievers mistake it for grounds to feel safe; they should be grateful, yet mock the warnings and presume their wealth is their birthright.
rows.anchor: The Almighty does not seize them immediately on their misdeeds and continues to give them respite.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diversity of human forms shows that God created each person in a distinct mould.
rows.anchor: each person was made in a different mould with different looks

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for proportion refers to balance and proportion, which the author connects to humanity’s creation in the finest mould.
rows.anchor: balance and proportion mentioned in the verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity reflects God’s brilliant creativity and must pass through tests to its appointed fate; refusal to face that responsibility merits punishment.
rows.anchor: a reflection of the brilliant creativity of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human midpoint among creations makes people worthy of vicegerency and the status of the middle community; fulfilling this duty merits the eternal kingdom of Heaven.
rows.anchor: is worthy of being made the vicegerent of God on earth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variety of faces and forms demonstrates God’s creative skill, since people were shaped differently without difficulty.
rows.anchor: each person was made in a different mould with different looks

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who creates people effortlessly will distinguish the righteous from wrongdoers and raise humanity again with equal ease.
rows.anchor: will raise up mankind once again without the slightest of difficulty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic rejection rebuts doubts about Judgment with the preceding evidence of God’s attributes in human creation; the opponents raise artificial objections because they do not want to believe.
rows.anchor: refute the doubts and objections

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reward and punishment accord with reason, human nature, justice, and God’s mercy and wisdom, so recreating people poses no difficulty for Him.
rows.anchor: how is it difficult for God to recreate man?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh knew denying reward and punishment meant denying something obvious, yet would neither accept it nor acknowledge it, so they invented baseless doubts.
rows.anchor: The disbelievers of the Quraysh found themselves in such a situation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God appoints guardians over every person to record words and deeds, including what people do openly and secretly, for later accountability.
rows.anchor: the Almighty has appointed guardians on each and every person who are noting each and every word and deed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the angels noble emphasizes their diligent, responsible, and impartial performance; they are neither negligent nor susceptible to pressure, cajoling, or inducement.
rows.anchor: full diligence, responsibility and impartiality.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse mentions the angels knowing deeds, while Qāf 50:18 explicitly says every spoken word is recorded.
rows.anchor: each word he utters shall be noted down by a vigilant guardian

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāf further describes two angels guarding a person, one on the right and one on the left.
rows.anchor: these angels are two in number and guard a person from his right and from his left.

rows.speaker: Certain narratives
rows.claim: Some narratives assign the two angels separate tasks: one records a person’s good deeds and the other their bad deeds.
rows.anchor: Certain narratives also speak of their division in labour: one of them writes the virtues of a person and the other his vices.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s care means He will distinguish the righteous from wrongdoers and reward or punish each; denying the afterlife or expecting deities’ intercession to secure luxuries ignores divine justice.
rows.anchor: justice and fairness have no place.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched will enter Hell on Judgment Day and remain there forever; anyone expecting to escape once there should abandon that notion.
rows.anchor: they will remain in it forever

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the hope that people might gain greater luxuries after death through the intercession of their deities.
rows.anchor: equally naïve are those who dream that

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular address is not to the Prophet but to the people addressed in 82:6 and afterward; singular address to a plural audience is an eloquent device.
rows.anchor: plural entities in the singular.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the previous question was rhetorical and meant to portray the Day’s terror, the final verse gives the answer immediately without waiting for a reply.
rows.anchor: Since the question raised in the previous verse was not meant to elicit an answer but to only portray the dread and horror of that day

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that Day no soul can benefit another; all affairs belong to God.
rows.anchor: no one would be of an y benefit to any other

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deities treated as God’s partners or intercessors, and worshipped in hopes of rescue, will have no power to save anyone from God.
rows.anchor: save people from the grasp of God
